evidence:
refs.bib currently has no Olah, Elhage or Sharkey entry, so the sentence has no citation. I checked it with grep.

(1) Elhage et al. 2022, Toy Models of Superposition (Transformer Circuits Thread, page fetched):
- The Open Questions section asks: "How many features should we expect to be stored in superposition? ... results from compressed sensing should be able to give us useful upper-bounds, but it would be nice to have a clearer understanding – and perhaps tighter bounds!"
- The main text says: "one question is just how many features the model learns to represent" (measured by ||W||_F^2).
- The SAE replication section says: "we ultimately want to count the features used by real neural networks, where the number of features is unknown."

(2) Sharkey et al. 2025, Open Problems in Mechanistic Interpretability (arXiv 2501.16496, fetched HTML), Sec. 2.1 on reverse-engineering/decomposition. It says conceptual work "may ... provide bounds on the number of features we should expect models to be capable of learning (Hänni et al., 2024; Adler & Shavit, 2024; Bushnaq & Mendel, 2024)".

(3) Olah et al. 2020, Zoom In (Distill, doi 10.23915/distill.00024.001), Claim 1: "Features are the fundamental unit of neural networks." This supports only that features are central.

Assessment: the question is explicitly posed as open, so the sentence is supported in substance. "Long-desired result" overstates things, though. The question has been posed since about 2022, and in mech interp "number of features" means superposition capacity or SAE feature counts, not Fourier frequencies or irreps. Search method: fetched the arXiv/Distill/transformer-circuits pages and grepped the full texts for "how many features" and "number of features". Notes: /Users/ruhaanrajadhyaksha/projects/grok/heracles/paper/litcheck/items/f1-long-desired/CHECK.md

recommended_citations.why: Supports abstract sentence 1. Its Open Questions section asks 'How many features should we expect to be stored in superposition?' and calls for tighter bounds. It also states 'we ultimately want to count the features used by real neural networks'.

Sec. 2.1 lists as an open problem the need to 'provide bounds on the number of features we should expect models to be capable of learning'. This directly supports calling the question open in the field.
Optional. Claim 1, 'Features are the fundamental unit of neural networks', supports the idea that features are central. It does not ask about how many there are.

recommended_change: Replace abstract sentence 1 with: "How many features a network learns is a central open question in mechanistic interpretability \citep{elhage2022superposition,sharkey2025open}." (Olah et al. 2020 is optional and supports only the notion of a feature.) Drop "long-desired result". In the intro, add one clause linking superposition-style feature counts to this paper's features (Fourier frequencies/irreps), so the framing does not suggest mech interp asked for exactly this.
